title: Posterior all-ceramic resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses made from Zirconia ceramic with minimally or non-invasive procedures
summary:
Missing  premolars due to caries, periodontal problems or congenitally missing ones can lead to chewing instability and aesthetic deficits. Such missing teeth are usually replaced by a fixed dental prothesis or an implant. The fabrication of a fixed dental prothesis goes along with a significant loss of tooth substance from the adjacent teeth, while implant placement requires a surgical intervention. Resin-bonded fixed dental prothesis (RBFDP), in which a cantilever is bonded to an abutment tooth, show excellent results for replacement of a missing anterior tooth when the adjacent tooth is free of fillings and caries. There is no evidence for RBFDPs in the posterior region.
This study aims to show the effectiveness of RBFDBs in the posterior region with minimally or no preparation of the abutment tooth.
In this investigation 30 RBFDPs are used to replace a premolar, 15 with minimally preparation and 15 without preparation. A maximum of two RBFDPs can be inserted per patient.
conditions: Diseases of oral cavity, salivary glands and jaws

interventions.name:
Patients will receive a posterior all-ceramic resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses (RBFDP) made from multilayer zirconia ceramic for replacement of a missing premolar. No tooth preparation will be performed except for the removal of undercuts, if necessary. All RBFDPs will be adhesively cemented.

Patients will receive an RBFDP made from multilayer zirconia ceramic for replacement of a missing premolar. The abutment tooth will be prepared following the guidelines for a minimal invasive tooth preparation for RBFDPs. All RBFDPs will be adhesively cemented.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
at least average oral hygiene
maximum 2 restorations per patient, no direct antagonists
periodontally healthy abutment teeth with no caries or fillings
premolar space not larger than 7 mm
no relocation is planned for the trial duration
Exclusion criteria:
pregnant or nursing women
